correctness.rationale: For each triangular block, one selected vertex is necessary to dominate its private vertex and at most one is possible because the block is a clique. Selected interior cut vertices correspond bijectively to disjoint dimers of the triangle-index path; all remaining triangles are monomers, with exactly two choices for an unmatched first/last endpoint and one internally. This directly proves the endpoint-weighted matching polynomial. Expanding endpoint factors gives p_n=f_n+2f_(n-1)+f_(n-2), and path matching recurrence gives p_2=4+t,p_3=4+4t,p_n=p_(n-1)+t p_(n-2) for n>=4. After z^n/4 transformation this equals characteristic polynomial of the Jacobi path with squared edge weights 1/4,3/4,1,...; symmetric irreducible tridiagonal theory proves simple real paired eigenvalues of magnitude <2 and the factorization. Independent exact graph brute force compared all 699048 candidate subsets on n=1..9; tiling vs generating-function vs determinant coefficients were checked for n=2..80. Infinite proof does not rest on enumeration.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2022 source already determines every coefficient of the triangular-chain enumerator, so enumeration or minimum cardinality is not presented as new. The submitted uniform endpoint-weighted matching bijection, particular Jacobi path with edge-square weights (1/4,3/4,1,...), and theorem that all nonzero roots for every n>=2 are simple and in (-4,0), together with log-concavity, were not identified in the closely read 2019 and 2022 originals or focused indexed searches. The uniform root conclusion needs a nontrivial structural step beyond reading off any fixed coefficient. Originality is a qualified self-review, not certification; the strong prior generating function is explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: A natural graph-counting polynomial family previously had complete coefficient formulas but not a proved simple-negative-root theorem; the new matching bijection explains its generating function and places every zero in a strict universal interval through explicit weighted-path Jacobi matrices. This yields Newton log-concavity and unimodality for all chain lengths, meaningful information about distribution shape and spectral structure not supplied by the earlier counting table. The case is not an arbitrary small graph or mere recomputation of known coefficients; root geometry is uniform in n.
